classification.tone: Wry, propulsive, grounded, and character-forward with a polished caper sheen

evaluation.positioning_hook: A British fixer is pulled back by an old friend to help steal a Monaco fortune, then discovers the job is cover for exposing a years-long corporate fraud.

audience_appeal_marketability.reasoning: The premise has immediate commercial traction: a globe-trotting heist, a charismatic crew, and a late reveal that the money is only the cover for a public takedown. The Monaco/Ferrari/vault engine gives the movie a clean sell, while the final Meridian exposure broadens the emotional payoff beyond the caper.

conceptual_hook_clarity.reasoning: The hook lands early in the New York bar scene and stays legible: Liam is recruited to get close to Damian, then the mission expands into a Monaco theft and a larger truth campaign. The script keeps the objective clear even as it layers in the real reason for the operation.

character_appeal_and_long_term_potential.reasoning: Liam, Damian, and Eleanor all have playable contradiction baked in, and the crew each has a distinct function and voice. Damian’s controlled intensity, Liam’s dry restraint, and Rico/Felix/Milo’s friction create a cast actors can lean into.

creative_originality_and_boldness.reasoning: The material is built on familiar heist architecture, but the corporate-reckoning motive and the specific crew chemistry give it a sharper identity than a standard theft movie. The choice to make the vault job a vehicle for whistleblowing adds a more adult, morally charged frame.

narrative_momentum_engagement.reasoning: The script moves with strong forward pressure: recruitment, crew assembly, Europe travel, the Monaco operation, the Switzerland leg, and the Hollywood Hills endgame all escalate cleanly. The set pieces are arranged to keep the audience leaning in, especially the wrong-vault beat and the final live transmission.

resonant_originality.reasoning: The core idea feels fresh because the heist is not the point; the heist is the delivery system for a truth campaign. The combination of precision-crime mechanics, corporate exposure, and a friendship-driven moral center gives the premise a memorable aftertaste.

world_density_and_texture.reasoning: The script moves through New York, Los Angeles, Rome, Sardinia, Monaco, Switzerland, and the Hollywood Hills with specific operational texture in each place. The world of private banking, estate security, logistics, and covert finance feels story-generating rather than decorative.

tonal_specificity.reasoning: The voice is distinct: dry, lightly comic, and highly competent, with characters who joke under pressure without losing the seriousness of the mission. The tone balances caper banter, procedural precision, and moral urgency in a way that feels ownable.

latent_depth_slow_burn_potential.reasoning: The surface pleasure is the job, but the deeper engine is Damian’s father, Meridian, and the question of what justice looks like when institutions refuse it. That gives the script a second life beneath the caper mechanics and makes the ending feel earned rather than merely clever.

relationship_density_and_ensemble_engine.reasoning: The ensemble is one of the script’s strongest assets: Damian/Liam carries the emotional spine, while Rico/Felix/Milo/Eleanor/Andrea all generate distinct pairings and group dynamics. The bar scenes, travel scenes, and planning rooms all prove that almost any two characters can carry a scene.

casting_characteristics: Specific age ranges for the crew and antagonists

locations.interior_exterior_ratio: Roughly 60/40 interior-heavy with key exterior travel and operation sequences
notable_requirements: Los Angeles diner, docks, tech center, parking garage, safe house, Hollywood Hills mansion
Monaco streets, estate, docks, and race-day exteriors
Swiss bank interiors and safe house chalet

technical.vfx_details: Mostly practical geography and crowd extension; race-day atmosphere, helicopter presence, and some surveillance/monitoring screens.
technical.sfx_needs: Controlled door charges, breakaway glass, fight choreography, vault mechanics, and practical explosion beats.

rights_flags.detail: Ferrari 250 GTO, Chubb door, Crédit Riviera bank, Formula One/Grand Prix references, Audi, Aperol, and named luxury/financial brands.
Meridian Group is fictional, but the Monaco Grand Prix setting and real-world luxury brands may require clearance depending on depiction.

platform_fit.recommended_lane: Premium streaming or theatrical-capable mid-budget crime thriller
platform_fit.series_engine_or_release_model: Feature release model with strong festival-to-platform or limited theatrical upside

cost.note: The story is dialogue- and planning-forward, but Monaco race-day exteriors, Europe travel, multiple premium locations, and a luxury car heist push it above contained indie scale.

cast.note: The ensemble is manageable, but the project benefits from a strong lead package and several distinct supporting roles that need the right chemistry.

location.note: The script spans New York, Los Angeles, Rome, Sardinia, Monaco, Switzerland, and multiple specialized interiors, including race-day and bank environments.

content.note: Violence is controlled but present, with fights, armed intrusion, and criminal activity, while the language and adult subject matter keep it in mature territory.

rights.note: Several named brands and real-world luxury references appear prominently, including Ferrari, Monaco Grand Prix, and banking/luxury identifiers.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The crew chemistry is the engine.
strengths.what_it_means: This gives the movie a built-in ensemble appeal that can sell on character as much as plot, which is exactly what helps a mid-budget thriller travel. Actors who want a sharp, banter-rich group dynamic with clear roles will see this as a fun, prestige-adjacent caper package.
strengths.evidence: The bar meeting, the plane ride, the Sardinia planning room, and the repeated back-and-forth between Rico, Felix, Milo, Eleanor, Damian, and Liam.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The heist has a moral payload.
strengths.what_it_means: The theft is not just about money; it becomes a vehicle for exposing Meridian and returning stolen value, which broadens the audience beyond pure crime fans. Buyers looking for a thriller with a conscience and a clean public-interest hook will understand the upside immediately.
strengths.evidence: The final reveal that Monaco funds are cover for the Hollywood Hills recording and the Meridian documentation release.

strengths.dimension_or_area: Damian is a premium lead role.
strengths.what_it_means: The role offers an actor the kind of controlled, morally complicated center that can anchor a whole film and invite awards-adjacent attention. Mid-career dramatic leads who want intelligence, restraint, and a late-film emotional reveal will chase this part.
strengths.evidence: Damian’s quiet planning scenes, his history with his father, and the jail-cell monologue that reframes the entire operation.

strengths.dimension_or_area: Liam gives the audience an entry point.
strengths.what_it_means: He functions as the audience proxy without feeling generic, which makes the movie accessible while keeping the world specialized. Actors who excel at dry wit and contained intensity will see a role that can play both observer and operator.
strengths.evidence: His first bar scene with the FBI, his deadpan reactions to the crew, and his physical competence in the Zurich bathroom and Hollywood Hills sequence.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The world feels operational, not decorative.
strengths.what_it_means: The script understands how private security, vault access, logistics, and surveillance actually shape a job, which gives the movie a credibility moat. Producers who want a thriller that feels smart on the page and producible on screen will respond to that specificity.
strengths.evidence: Camera loops, vault schematics, sewer exits, race-day cover, and the Swiss banking sequence.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The tone has a clean signature.
strengths.what_it_means: The script can sit in the lane of sophisticated adult entertainment: funny under pressure, but never winking away the stakes. That makes it attractive to directors and buyers who want a crime film with polish, wit, and emotional seriousness.
strengths.evidence: The repeated jokes about left/right, the bar banter, and the way the team jokes while executing serious operations.

strengths.what_it_means: The final act doesn’t just resolve the caper; it turns the movie into a public reckoning, which gives the project a stronger afterlife in marketing and word of mouth. Buyers who want a thriller with a topical tailwind and a satisfying reveal will see the value in that structure.
strengths.evidence: The Hollywood Hills recording goes live, the Meridian story breaks, and the final news montage shows the fallout.

whats_special.headline: PROJECT CROSS is a polished, adult heist thriller with a strong ensemble, a charismatic central duo, and a mission that expands from luxury theft into public exposure. It has the kind of globe-spanning, character-driven momentum that can attract both prestige-minded talent and commercial buyers looking for a smart, producible crime package.

lead_characters.name: LIAM CARTER
lead_characters.hook: Liam is the calm, dryly funny outsider who reads rooms faster than he reveals himself. He looks like a man trying to stay one step removed from the chaos, but the script keeps proving he can operate inside it with real precision, which makes him both the audience’s guide and the team’s quiet insurance policy.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Matthew Rhys in The Americans or Richard Madden in Bodyguard — a controlled, intelligent lead whose stillness is the performance. Actors who can play wit, restraint, and sudden physical competence will see a role that lets them carry a thriller without ever shouting for attention.

lead_characters.name: DAMIAN CROSS
lead_characters.hook: Damian is the architect of the whole operation: precise, private, and carrying a grievance so deep it has become a life plan. He’s not a swaggering thief; he’s a man who has turned memory, discipline, and anger into a mission, which gives him a rare combination of intelligence and emotional pressure.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase space of Oscar Isaac in A Most Violent Year or Michael Shannon in Take Shelter — a man whose inner weather is the story. Actors looking for a role that can play command, secrecy, and a late-film moral reveal will chase this immediately.

lead_characters.name: ELEANOR CROSS
lead_characters.hook: Eleanor is the forensic accountant who sees through people the way she sees through ledgers: quickly, accurately, and without sentimentality. She’s Damian’s fiancée, but she never reads as ornamental; she’s the one who grounds the mission in facts, pressure, and emotional truth.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role Rosamund Pike had in Gone Girl or Rebecca Ferguson in Mission: Impossible — a woman whose intelligence is the weapon and whose composure hides real force. Actors who want a sharp, adult, high-status part with both romantic and operational authority will want this.

lead_characters.name: RICO SANTORO
lead_characters.hook: Rico is the explosives specialist with the loudest opinions and the clearest standards, a guy who turns technical expertise into personality. He’s grumpy, funny, and weirdly principled, which makes him feel like the kind of professional every crew needs and every audience remembers.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase lane of Walton Goggins in Justified or Benicio del Toro in Sicario — a scene-stealing operator who can make expertise feel like charisma. Character actors who can play menace, humor, and loyalty in one package will chase it.

lead_characters.name: FELIX NOVAK
lead_characters.hook: Felix is the hyperactive tech brain of the crew, all speed, anxiety, and accidental brilliance. He’s funny because he’s specific, not because he’s comic relief, and the script gives him enough competence to feel essential while still letting his neuroses generate energy.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role Jesse Eisenberg had in The Social Network or Rami Malek in Mr. Robot — a fast-talking, high-functioning specialist whose brain is the spectacle. Younger actors with sharp timing and an edge of vulnerability will see a breakout part here.

lead_characters.name: MILO REYES
lead_characters.hook: Milo is the driver/mechanic who treats machines with more patience than people, and that tells you everything about him. He’s understated, observant, and quietly funny, with the kind of competence that makes him feel like the crew’s most reliable moving part.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Michael Peña in End of Watch or Shea Whigham in a prestige crime ensemble — a grounded, watchful role that rewards detail and timing. Actors who can make competence feel human will be drawn to it.

lead_characters.name: ANDREA CALCALE
lead_characters.hook: Andrea is the charmingly dangerous fixer with money, access, and the confidence to treat everyone else’s urgency as a scheduling issue. He’s funny, elegant, and slightly opaque, which makes him feel like a man who has built a life out of leverage and taste.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of supporting role that gives an actor the same pleasure as Javier Bardem in Skyfall or Stanley Tucci in The Lovely Bones — a polished, scene-owning presence with hidden depth. A-list character actors who enjoy making every entrance count will want this immediately.

lead_characters.name: AGENT THEADORE COLLINS
lead_characters.hook: Collins is the composed federal presence who understands the shape of a case and the shape of a room. He’s not flashy, but he has authority, patience, and the kind of controlled intelligence that makes him feel dangerous without ever raising his voice.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase lane of Jeffrey Wright in a procedural thriller or Shea Whigham in a federal drama — a role built on stillness, command, and subtext. Actors who specialize in authority with texture will be interested.

lead_characters.name: AGENT GABRIEL MORALES
lead_characters.hook: Morales is the more instinctive half of the FBI pair, the one who reads people as much as files. He carries the emotional temperature of the investigation, which gives him a humanizing tension against Collins’s colder certainty.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gives an actor the grounded moral pressure of Michael Peña in End of Watch or Diego Luna in Narcos. It’s a strong supporting part for someone who can play skepticism, empathy, and procedural urgency.

director_appeal.hook: A director who wants to make a smart, stylish crime film where character chemistry matters as much as the mechanics.
director_appeal.fit_profile: Established indie or prestige-leaning directors with at least one or two features, especially those who like ensemble blocking, procedural detail, and morally charged genre storytelling. This material rewards a filmmaker who can stage dialogue, travel, and operations with confidence while keeping the emotional center on Damian and Liam.
director_appeal.detail: The movie gives a director a chance to balance caper precision with a real human spine, and the set pieces are built around clarity rather than spectacle for spectacle’s sake. It will appeal to directors who like adult genre material that can play commercially without losing character nuance.

buyer_appeal.lane: Premium streamer / theatrical-capable adult thriller lane
buyer_appeal.detail: The ensemble is strong enough to package around a lead pair and a few high-value supporting roles, so it can be mounted without needing a giant star stack. The heist-plus-exposure structure gives buyers both a commercial crime hook and a topical truth-telling angle that plays well on streaming and in limited theatrical.

considerations.area: The opening takes its time before the mission engine locks in.
considerations.detail: The New York bar sequence is stylish and character-rich, but the script could consider bringing the Damian/Liam pressure point into view a little sooner so the audience feels the central engine earlier. The version where the recruitment tension arrives one beat faster would keep the same sophistication and sharpen the first-act pull.

considerations.area: The crew introductions run as a series of arrivals.
considerations.detail: The ensemble is appealing, and the individual voices are clear, but there is room to foreground one or two relationship pairings earlier so the group feels even more interconnected before the travel section. A next pass could let a single scene do double duty for character and mission setup, which would tighten the first half without changing the material.

considerations.area: The European travel footprint is expansive.
considerations.detail: The story moves through New York, Los Angeles, Rome, Sardinia, Monaco, Switzerland, and Hollywood Hills, which gives it scale but also asks a lot of the production plan. One simplification lever would be to see whether one of the European stops could absorb another function without losing the story’s momentum or texture.

considerations.area: The final reveal carries the movie’s deepest charge.
considerations.detail: The Meridian exposure is the emotional and thematic payoff, and the script already lands it cleanly; a future pass could consider seeding one additional image or line earlier that points toward the public-reckoning ending. That would make the last-act turn feel even more inevitable while preserving the surprise of the full plan.

considerations.area: The brand and location references are specific.
considerations.detail: Ferrari, Monaco Grand Prix, Chubb, Crédit Riviera, Audi, and Aperol all help the movie feel tangible, but they also create a clear clearance checklist. If the production wants more flexibility, the version of the script where a few of those identifiers are softened would preserve the same luxury-crime feel with less dependency on named elements.
